final_answer: Imagine a small town where every summer, a new ice cream truck arrives, and at the same time, the local hospital sees more sunburn cases. A visitor might think, "Eating ice cream causes sunburns!" But here's the twist: the real reason both happen is the weather. When it gets hotter, people buy more ice cream to cool off and spend more time outside, increasing their chance of sunburns. The ice cream and sunburns aren’t directly linked—they’re both reacting to the same hidden factor: the heat. This shows that just because two things happen together, it doesn’t mean one causes the other.
